round_1.spec: Dispatch primary document of LEGION-30, version 5 (Acceptance 1-7)
round_1.verdict_summary: Criteria 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 pass; criterion 6's pre-merge half is proven end to end on a throwaway daemon from the PR head (live half pending the operator's post-merge restart); criterion 1 FAILS on one ordering found by the rig: a worker whose idle-retire clock expired as a no-op while it was the issue's active phase is never re-armed when phases[issue] later moves to another role, so it stays resident indefinitely although every Acceptance-1 condition holds. One small fix plus one regression test; then re-test.

1.passes: steady-state orderings: past-window retire (phases absent / completed / other role) with one graceful shutdown frame, no kill-pane, locator cleared, resumeSessionFile carried, launchFailures/promptFailures untouched, zero publications; under-window, re-prompted, active-phase, queued-task, sub-architect untouched -- all by the 9 new tests (201 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail, 204 tests) and observed live on the rig (3 retirements, negative control resident).
1.fails: phase-moves-after-expiry ordering. Rig: reviewer was phases[LEGSMOKE-63]; its clock fired ~20:24:15Z as a correct no-op; at 20:25:32Z the retired planner was resumed via spawn_worker and its /worker/started re-wrote phases[LEGSMOKE-63]=planner (workers.ts:212); the reviewer -- idle since 20:22:43Z, no pendingAssignment, role != architect, tree active -- was still resident at 20:31:27Z (8.7 min idle, 5.7 min not the active phase) with no clock pending. Cause: armIdleRetire's map entry is deleted at expiry; retireIdleWorker returns without re-arming; only a worker's own idle transition arms a clock, and nothing runs when phases[issue] changes.
1.unit_repro: idleWorkerFixture({role:'reviewer', phases:{[root]:{phase:'reviewer',sessionId:'ses_reviewer'}}}); expect(clock.fire(600_000)).toBeTrue(); await flushEventLoop(20); state.phases[root]={phase:'planner',sessionId:'ses_planner'}; expect(clock.pending.filter(w=>w.ms===600_000)).toHaveLength(0) /* gap */; expect(clock.fire(600_000)).toBeFalse(); shutdownCalls stays [] and locator stays set. Ran as a throwaway copy of processes.test.ts (not committed): pending clocks = 0, retired = false.
1.proposed_fix: In retireIdleWorker, when the predicate declines for a reason that can change without this worker's own idle transition (active phase, pendingAssignment, closing tree) and this.workerClients.get(token) === client && client.runState === 'idle' && !this.disposed, call this.armIdleRetire(token, client) so the clock polls once per window until the phase moves. Regression test = the repro above with the inverse assertions after a second fire(600_000): one shutdown, locator cleared, resumeSessionFile set. Alternative: re-arm every cached idle client of the issue wherever phases[issue] is written (workers.ts:212, processes.ts:652, phase/complete).
1.real_world_shape: Any worker that ends a turn while still the recorded phase and is then superseded by another role's spawn -- e.g. a retro implementer that never calls `legion handoff complete` before the final reviewer is spawned -- leaks one resident omp process per issue until the tree closes. The operator sweep (retire-idle-workers.py) re-evaluates every 10 min and so would eventually catch it; the daemon's clock does not.

2.evidence: unit: 'resumes a retired worker with --resume on its next spawn_worker' (asserts --resume=<sessionFile>, generation 2, expectedSessionId, resumeSessionFile cleared, launchFailures 0). Rig: spawn_worker planner at 20:25:32Z -> daemon log '[legion] respawning LEGSMOKE-63 by resuming OMP session .../2026-09-12T20-22-13-694Z_01a09748-ebbe-7000-841c-ec6b9789f2be.jsonl'; pane_start_command carries --resume=<that file>; claim generation 2 with the same sessionId 01a09748-ebbe-7000-841c-ec6b9789f2be; the same session file then carries 'done' then 'resumed'.

3.evidence: unit: 'does not count a retired claim (locator cleared, resumeSessionFile kept) toward the running-worker cap' (workerCap 1, retired claim present, a new tester still launches, queue empty). Rig: after retirement the three claims are locator-less with resumeSessionFile and the reviewer/planner spawns were never queued (workerAdmission.queue=[]).

4.evidence: unit: 'never retires an idle sub-architect, however long its idle window has run'. Rig: the root architect claim (role architect, no worker locator) and the controller (not a worker claim) stayed resident for the whole 16-minute run; only planner/implementer/tester were retired. retireIdleWorker's `claim.role === 'architect'` and `!('issue' in claim)` guards are the reason.

5.evidence: config.test.ts 39 pass / 0 fail. CLI surface (`bun run src/cli/index.ts start tester/c5 --config <tmp legion.yaml> --checkConfig`, LEGION_*/DISPATCH_*/ENVOY_* scrubbed from env): yaml 600 -> 'Config OK'; yaml 0 -> 'Config OK'; yaml -1 -> exit 1 'error: worker_idle_retire_seconds must be a non-negative integer'; yaml 1.5 -> exit 1 same text; yaml "abc" -> exit 1 'error: worker_idle_retire_seconds must be a finite number'; env LEGION_WORKER_IDLE_RETIRE_SECONDS=0 -> 'Config OK'; =90 -> 'Config OK'; =-1 / =1.5 / =abc -> exit 1 'error: LEGION_WORKER_IDLE_RETIRE_SECONDS must be a non-negative integer'; no key -> 'Config OK' (default 600 asserted by the unit test; --checkConfig prints only the project). Precedence YAML>env>default is unit-covered.
